At iso-conversion conditions (26% 1-butene cracking conversion), the M2 catalyst exhibited markedly enhanced olefin selectivity with negligible paraffin and aromatic formation compared to M1. This behavior supports the hypothesis that reduced electronegativity of oxygen in M- OH species decreases transition state stabilization, shifting product distribution toward olefins. A comprehensive analytical system was established using an Aatar Effi microreactor (425-600 μm catalyst particles) with integrated flow and temperature control, coupled to online gas chromatography through heated transfer lines. The GC method was calibrated for C1-C10 compound identification, enabling accurate quantification of paraffins, olefins, and BTX aromatics. CD CN FT-IR spectroscopy confirmed acid site speciation, with distinct peaks corresponding to different Brønsted acid environments. This characterization provided₃ the foundation for a mechanistic understanding of catalyst performance. Milestone 4.4.2: Obtain >70% yields of monomers from thermal depolymerization of actual plastic waste using optimized zeolites in a continuous flow reactor for 100 hours on stream with intermediate regeneration in a reactor that processes 5 mL/day was successfully completed on March 30, 2025, exceeding the target of 70% monomer yields. The project demonstrated 100-hour continuous operation of post-consumer waste polypropylene (PCW-PP) pyrolysis oil upgrading with intermediate catalyst regeneration, achieving 88% overall conversion and 69% selectivity to plastic monomers (paraffins, olefins, and aromatics). The continuous flow fixed-bed reactor processed PCW-PP pyrolysis oil at 1.0-2.5 mL/h over 0.25 g H/ZSM-5 (Si/Al = 15) catalyst at 500 °C with 150 mL/min N carrier gas. Initial deactivation studies over 15 hours showed conversion declining to approximately 50% with 40% monomer selectivity, informing the selection of 6-hour rea₂ction cycles to maintain yields above 60-70%. The reactor was modified to include an ice-cooled trap for offline analysis of heavy fractions using calibrated GC methods. Over the 100-hour campaign, 17 reaction cycles were completed with 16 intermediate regeneration steps. Product distribution remained relatively stable throughout the test period, with selectivity toward paraffins, olefins, and BTX aromatics measured at 2-hour intervals. The reactor system successfully processed more than 5 mL/day of pyrolysis oil, meeting the SOPO requirement while maintaining target conversion and selectivity levels. Milestone 4.4.3: Demonstrate catalyst regeneration to regain >90% of the original catalyst activity was successfully completed through optimized regeneration protocols. This achievement required systematic investigation of regeneration conditions, including temperature, atmosphere composition, and treatment duration. Initial regeneration attempts at 500°C with 10% O in N (150 mL/min total flow) for 12 hours proved insufficient, leaving visible coke deposits and reduced selectivity recovery. Progressive optimization evaluated five distin₂ct pro₂tocols. Condition (a) used 500°C with 10% O , achieving incomplete regeneration. Condition (b) employed a step-wise temperature increase to 550 °C (11 hours) followed by 650 °C (1 hour), showing improvement bu₂t incomplete recovery. Condition (c) maintained 600 °C for 12 hours with marginal gains. A breakthrough occurred with condition (d), combining a temperature increase to 700 °C with enhanced oxygen concentration (20% O , 15 mL/min) and reduced total flow (75 mL/min). This protocol nearly restored full catalyst activity.
